topic_name: The Language of Culture and the Typology of Signs

101.question: How does the main emphasis of hermeneutics differ from that of semiotics?

options.A: Hermeneutics studies understanding, semiotics studies sign structure
options.B: Hermeneutics excludes interpretation, semiotics excludes signs
options.C: Hermeneutics studies the physics of sound, semiotics studies genealogy
options.D: Hermeneutics studies the norms of law, semiotics studies the norms of morality
options.E: Hermeneutics studies only writing, semiotics studies only oral speech

102.question: The following processes belong to the hermeneutic mastery of culture:

options.A: Cognition
options.B: Encoding
options.C: Understanding
options.D: Signification
options.E: Experiencing (lived experience)

103.question: What do the various means of the language of culture have in common?

options.A: They function exclusively in a written tradition
options.B: They necessarily have a verbal form
options.C: They make it possible to orient oneself in cultural space and to convey meanings
options.D: They presuppose a single alphabet common to all cultures
options.E: They eliminate the need for interpretation

104.question: Indicate the characteristics of the sign that C. S. Peirce singled out.

options.A: An innate connection between the carrier and the meaning
options.B: A link with use and understanding
options.C: Obligatory iconic resemblance
options.D: Material expression
options.E: Self-identity of the sign and the object it denotes

105.question: Smoke serves as an indication of fire by virtue of a causal link. To which type does such a sign belong?

options.A: Natural
options.B: Functional
options.C: Verbal
options.D: Conventional
options.E: Iconic

106.question: A machine part tells a researcher about a technical system by virtue of its practical purpose. This is a ... sign.

options.A: Verbal
options.B: Functional
options.C: Iconic
options.D: Written-alphabet element
options.E: Conventional signal

107.question: The sound imitation of sea waves in music is an example of a(n) ... sign.

options.A: Iconic
options.B: Alphabetic notation
options.C: Functional indicator
options.D: Verbal
options.E: Conventional index

108.question: At the basis of the meaning of a conventional sign lies...

options.A: A social agreement about the meaning
options.B: An outward resemblance to the thing denoted
options.C: A natural causal connection with the object
options.D: The practical function of an object in activity
options.E: An inherited psychophysiological reaction

options.A: Iconic signs
options.B: Functional signs
options.C: Indices
options.D: Symbols
options.E: Signals

110.question: A sign that is specifically meant to notify or warn is called a...

options.A: Symbol
options.B: Functional sign
options.C: Index
options.D: Iconic sign
options.E: Signal

111.question: A compact conventional designation of an object or situation on a diagram is a(n)...

options.A: Index
options.B: Functional sign
options.C: Signal
options.D: Symbol
options.E: Iconic sign

112.question: The feature that distinguishes a symbol among signs is...

options.A: The presence of an exclusively sound carrier
options.B: The absence of a connection with collective experience
options.C: The expression of an additional value-laden meaning
options.D: Obligatory literal resemblance to the object
options.E: A single unchanging interpretation

113.question: Why can a pair of scales express the idea of justice?

options.A: The idea of balance creates an associative link between the form and the value-laden meaning
options.B: Any connection between the design of the scales and the symbolic meaning is ruled out
options.C: The legal meaning is derived from the material of the pans
options.D: Their mass is physically equal to moral worth
options.E: Any measuring instrument automatically signifies justice

114.question: Indicate the correct "example: type of symbol" pairs.

options.A: The cross: a religious symbol
options.B: The colour white as purity: a moral symbol
options.C: The field of Borodino as military glory: a verbal system of notation
options.D: Scales as justice: a historical symbol
options.E: A state slogan: a natural indicative sign

115.question: How are the biological prerequisites and the social nature of spoken language related?

options.A: Joint activity merely preserves an unchanging innate grammar
options.B: The biological organization passes on a ready-made vocabulary by inheritance
options.C: Language arises without communication as an individual reflex
options.D: The organs of speech create the possibility of language, but it develops in joint activity
options.E: The social nature of language excludes the significance of hearing and the brain

116.question: A natural language is called an open system because...

options.A: Its vocabulary does not depend on the history of culture
options.B: It contains no stable elements
options.C: Every sign has only one permissible meaning
options.D: The rules of its construction are fully formalized
options.E: It is capable of unlimited development

117.question: The part of the vocabulary characterized by comparatively long-lasting stability is...

options.A: Names of body parts, celestial bodies and the simplest actions
options.B: Names of current fashionable trends
options.C: Designations of the latest technical devices
options.D: The lexicon of vanished narrow professions
options.E: Names of short-lived political campaigns

118.question: Writing and musical notation are called secondary sign systems because...

options.A: They arise on the basis of already existing language and music
options.B: They have less cultural value than oral speech
options.C: They are applicable exclusively to professional art
options.D: Their signs lack an independent material expression
options.E: They arise earlier than any forms of sound communication

119.question: Writing creates the following possibilities for cultural memory:

options.A: Preserving ideas until interested descendants appear
options.B: The automatic preservation of a single authorial interpretation
options.C: Transmission of a ready-made meaning independently of the cultural code
options.D: Replacement of teaching between generations by genetic inheritance
options.E: The accumulation of rarely used vocabulary

120.question: Strict formalization of the rules of construction is most characteristic of...

options.A: The artificial languages of logic and mathematics
options.B: The oral performance of folklore
options.C: Spontaneous gestural expressiveness
options.D: The symbolic polysemy of an artistic image
options.E: The spoken language of everyday communication

121.question: Myth, religion and art as communication structures belong...

options.A: To the formal languages of computation
options.B: To natural spoken languages
options.C: To secondary languages
options.D: To biological signals
options.E: To alphabetic systems of notation

122.question: Which new possibility do written signs provide in the account of the evolution of communication?

options.A: Transmission of ready-made cultural meanings through DNA
options.B: The disappearance of the need for a material carrier
options.C: The abandonment of the accumulation of intergenerational experience
options.D: The preservation of culture in the extragenetic memory of humankind
options.E: The restriction of communication to direct oral contact

123.question: It is true of the model sign in the mythological cultural code that...

options.A: It stores information about the meaning of an object and the ways of acting with it
options.B: It denies the possibility of substituting for real action
options.C: It excludes the endowing of an object with magical power
options.D: It necessarily represents only a natural symptom
options.E: It is reduced to a literal enumeration of the parts of an object

124.question: The cultural-studies investigation of a symbol includes the following tasks:

options.A: Reducing all symbols to unambiguous technical signals
options.B: Identifying the symbolic form with a physical property of the carrier
options.C: Studying a deliberately created symbolic message
options.D: Interpreting a meaning attributed to an object without deliberate intent
options.E: Establishing an unchanging natural meaning of any image

125.question: The formula "the unity of allusion and concealment", which characterizes the symbol, is associated with the name of...

options.A: L. Wittgenstein
options.B: C. S. Peirce
options.C: E. Tylor
options.D: C. Lévi-Strauss
options.E: H.-G. Gadamer
